overall.verdict: Major Interaction and Patient-Safety Alert Flagged
overall.summary: Patient-safety alert: Therapeutic duplication: Aspirin + Ibuprofen are both NSAIDs (including aspirin). Your medicines—warfarin, aspirin, and ibuprofen—have major interactions that can cause serious bleeding and other health problems. Being 65 or older makes these risks higher. Talk with your doctor or pharmacist about these concerns.

alerts.label: Major / Therapeutic Duplication (Same Drug Class)
alerts.title: Therapeutic duplication: Aspirin + Ibuprofen are both NSAIDs (including aspirin)
alerts.detail: Stacking NSAIDs adds up stomach ulcer, bleeding, kidney and heart risks without giving more pain relief. Ask the prescriber whether both are really needed.

explanation.why: Taking two NSAIDs at the same time adds up the risk of stomach ulcers, bleeding, kidney injury, and heart problems without giving you more pain relief.

context_advice: Because you are over 65, you have a higher chance of bleeding and stomach problems from these drugs, so close monitoring and clear communication with your health‑care team are especially important.

drugs.boxed_warning: WARNING: BLEEDING RISK Warfarin sodium can cause major or fatal bleeding [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1) ] . Perform regular monitoring of INR in all treated patients [see Dosage and Administration (2.1) ] . Drugs, dietary changes, and other factors affect INR levels achieved with warfarin sodium therapy [see Drug Interactions (7) ] . Instruct patients about prevention measures to minimize risk of bleeding and to report signs and symptoms of bleeding [see Patient Counseling Information (17) ] . drugs.name: ibuprofen
drugs.boxed_warning: Cardiovascular Thrombotic Events Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) cause an increased risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events, including myocardial infarction and stroke, which can be fatal. This risk may occur early in treatment and may increase with duration of use [see Warnings and Precautions ]. Ibuprofen tablets are contraindicated in the setting of coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery [see Contraindications and Warnings ]. label_hits.text: This product contains an NSAID, which may cause severe stomach bleeding.
Preexisting asthma Patients with asthma may have aspirin-sensitive asthma.
The use of aspirin in patients with aspirin-sensitive asthma has been associated with severe bronchospasm, which can be fatal.

Since cross reactivity, including bronchospasm, between aspirin and NSAIDs has been reported in such aspirin-sensitive patients, ibuprofen tablets should not be administered to patients with this form of aspirin sensitivity and should be used with caution in patients with preexisting asthma.
There is no consistent evidence that concurrent use of aspirin mitigates the increased risk of serious CV thrombotic events associated with NSAID use.
The concurrent use of aspirin and an NSAID, such as ibuprofen, increases the risk of serious gastrointestinal (GI) events [ see Warnings ].

explanation.why: Both are NSAIDs; using them together adds up the risk of stomach ulcers, bleeding, kidney problems, and can reduce aspirin’s heart‑protective effect.
explanation.timing: They should not be taken at the same time; discuss with your provider whether you need one, the other, or a different medication.
